title: Existence of finite-stage data for a finite-type morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be locally of finite type, with $X$ and $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Choose Noetherian approximations $\mathsf N(X)$ and $\mathsf N(S)$ [def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system], indexed by small cofiltered categories in the schemes' universe, with projections $p_i:X\to X_i$ and $q_s:S\to S_s$. Given any prescribed source and target stages, there are stages $i,s$ admitting arrows to the prescribed stages and a morphism $\varphi:X_i\to S_s$ such that
$$
\varphi\circ p_i=q_s\circ f.
$$
The induced comparison $c=(p_i,f):X\to X_i\times_{S_s}S$ is an immersion (a closed immersion into an open subscheme of the fibre product). These choices extend to a finite-stage datum of [def-nagata-relative-stage-morphism-data]: one can record finite affine charts, finite generator-and-relation presentations and chart maps for the finite-type-over-$\mathbf Z$ stages, their finite overlap compatibility data, and a finite affine cover of $X$ with compatible affine opens in $X_i\times_{S_s}S$ on which the comparison is induced by surjective ring maps. The base-changed stage morphism recovers $f$ by composition with $c$, namely $\mathrm{pr}_S\circ c=f$; no isomorphism $X\cong X_i\times_{S_s}S$ is asserted. Finiteness of the presentations concerns the stage charts, and does not assert that the kernels of the comparison's surjective ring maps are finitely generated.

proof.text: Noetherian approximations exist for both qcqs schemes by prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system; fix the chosen systems. Choose the target stage $s$ to be the prescribed one. Its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally of finite presentation: it is locally of finite type by the definition of approximation, and apply pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth. Here $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally Noetherian according to pqf-def-locnoeth: every nonzero ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is generated by its least positive element (division with remainder leaves an element of the ideal smaller than that element), and the zero ideal is generated by $0$. Thus the definition of a Noetherian ring applies. Apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-map-limit-factorization over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to $q_s f:X\to S_s$ and the source system, obtaining $j$ and $g:X_j\to S_s$ with $g p_j=q_s f$. Its stages are qcqs and transitions affine by the approximation hypotheses. All scheme morphisms commute with their maps to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text: By the definition of locally finite type, for every point of $X$ choose an affine neighbourhood $V_a$ mapping into an affine open $U_a\subset S$, with $C_a=\Gamma(V_a,\mathcal O_X)$ a finitely generated algebra over $A_a=\Gamma(U_a,\mathcal O_S)$. Quasi-compactness of $X$ selects finitely many such pairs covering $X$. Choose finite algebra generators $z_{ab}\in C_a$. Descend each affine open $V_a$ to an affine open in a source stage by lem-trf-affine-open-limit-descent. Take a common predecessor $k$ of $j$, the prescribed source stage, and the finitely many stages just obtained. Cofilteredness supplies it by induction on this finite list. Pull the descended opens back to affine opens $T_a\subset X_k$; affineness follows from the affine transition maps and pqf-def-affine-morphism. Cone identities give $p_k^{-1}T_a=V_a$. The $T_a$ need only cover the image of $X$, not all of $X_k$.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text: Apply lem-nagata-cofiltered-finite-affine-sections-lift to the source system, stage $k$, and the finite family indexed by pairs $(a,b)$, with open $T_a$ and function $z_{ab}$. Obtain one arrow $l\to k$ and lifts $\widetilde z_{ab}$ on the inverse-image affine opens $T'_a\subset X_l$. Define $\varphi:X_l\to S_s$ to be $g$ composed with the transition $X_l\to X_j$. Then $\varphi p_l=q_s f$ by the cone identity. The arrow $l\to k$ followed by the previously chosen arrow to the prescribed source stage supplies the required enlargement. Each $p_l^{-1}T'_a=V_a$.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text:
Put $Y=X_l\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}S$ and let $e=(p_l,f):X\to Y$. By lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, for each $a$ the product $O_a=T'_a\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U_a$ is an affine open in $Y$, with ring $B_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A_a$, where $B_a=\Gamma(T'_a,\mathcal O_{X_l})$. Its inverse image under $e$ is exactly $V_a$: the first component requires membership in $V_a$, and $f(V_a)\subset U_a$ supplies the second. Under the affine fibre-product identification the ring map is
$$b\otimes a\longmapsto p_l^\sharp(b)f^\sharp(a).$$
Its image contains $f^\sharp(A_a)$ and all $z_{ab}$, the latter as the images of $\widetilde z_{ab}\otimes1$. These generate $C_a$ as an $A_a$-algebra, so the map is surjective. This uses finite generation only, not finite presentation of $C_a$ over $A_a$.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text: Let $W=\bigcup_aO_a\subset Y$. The morphism $e$ factors through $W$, since the inverse images $V_a$ cover $X$. On the affine cover $(O_a)_a$ of $W$, each inverse image is affine and the section map is surjective by the preceding computation. The closed-immersion affine-cover criterion therefore makes $X\to W$ a closed immersion. Composing with the open inclusion $W\to Y$ proves that $e$ is an immersion, by the definition of immersion.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text: Let $P=X_l\times_{S_s}S$ and $c=(p_l,f):X\to P$, using the equality $\varphi p_l=q_sf$. The two projections from $P$ define $M:P\to Y$; on both components $M c=e$, hence this equality follows from the fibre-product universal property. Immersion cancellation applied to $M c$ gives that $c$ is an immersion. Choose an open $W'\subset P$ into which $c$ is a closed immersion. Cover $W'$ by affine opens and, using the quasi-compactness of $X$, retain finitely many whose inverse images cover $X$. Those inverse images are affine and their coordinate maps are surjective by clause (1) of the closed-immersion affine-cover criterion. These are the required immersion-chart witnesses. No affine-intersection assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text:
Record finite chart data for $\varphi$. The stage structure morphisms over $\mathbf Z$ are locally of finite presentation by pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth, hence have affine charts with finitely presented $\mathbf Z$ coordinate algebras. First choose finitely many target charts. Refine source presentation charts inside their inverse images by principal opens, which form the affine Zariski basis: an open neighbourhood of a prime contains $D(b)$ for some element $b$ outside that prime. Clause (0) of lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme identifies a principal-open coordinate ring with $B[1/b]$. If $B=\mathbf Z[y_1,\ldots,y_r]/(q_1,\ldots,q_t)$ and $\widetilde b$ represents $b$, then
$$B[1/b]\cong\mathbf Z[y_1,\ldots,y_r,z]/(q_1,\ldots,q_t,z\widetilde b-1):$$
the maps send $z$ to $b^{-1}$ and a fraction $v/b^n$ to $v z^n$, and are inverse by the localization relations. Thus this refinement retains finite presentations. Compactness selects a finite refining source cover. For a chart map $\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\to B$, record the images of the finitely many $x_i$, represented by polynomials in the finite presentation of $B$, and the equations $r_t\mapsto0$. There are finitely many coefficients and equations. This records the existing map $\varphi$; it does not assert finite presentation of $X/S$.

source.place: Tag 01ZE, label lemma-locally-finite-type-in-finite-presentation, proof; combined with Tag 01ZC, label proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3)

proof.text: To record overlaps, use finite affine refinements of pairwise and triple intersections of the finitely many stage charts, as in the finite affine gluing presentation. Such intersections are quasi-compact because the stages are Noetherian; use the affine-open basis to select finite affine covers, without asserting that an intersection itself is affine. Choose these refinements by principal opens in the stage charts, so their finite presentations are supplied by the explicit localization calculation of step 7. Record the restrictions of $\varphi$ on these refinements and their compatibility equalities. They agree because they are restrictions of the single morphism $\varphi$; on each finitely presented chart algebra equality is determined by the finite list of generators. The finite lists of charts, maps, generator images, and equations, together with the surjections of step 6, are precisely the additional records required in def-nagata-relative-stage-morphism-data. Finally the fibre-product equation gives $\mathrm{pr}_S c=f$, so restricting the base-changed chart maps along these comparison charts gives the original morphism. This assembles the datum.

blueprint_update.statement:
If $S$ is qcqs and $X\to S$ is locally of finite type with $X$
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then a finite-stage datum exists after enlarging both
indices. Its chart maps use only finitely many coefficients and relations,
and their base change to $S$ is the original morphism.

proof.text:
Choose finite affine presentations of source and target charts. Their
finitely many coefficients, structural maps, and overlap identities occur
at one common stage by the finite-data lemma; enlarging both indices gives
the required compatible datum and immersion charts.

Q122's parallel split of def-nagata-relative-stage-morphism-data leaves the definition's statement unchanged. STATEMENT: the old wording 'base change to S is the original morphism' is false. Counterexample: Spec k -> Spec k[x1,x2,...] is a closed immersion of finite type but not of finite presentation, while any base change of a morphism between finite-type-over-Z stages is of finite presentation. The new statement (phi p_i = q_s f; c=(p_i,f) is an immersion; finite chart, presentation and overlap records; surjective immersion charts; pr_S c = f) is exactly what the definition asks for and what the only citer, def-nagata-immersion-into-fp-model, uses (Y = X_lambda x S). Nothing is weakened. The added 'small index' wording is a universe convention that the approximation construction already satisfies. STEPS: 1) exists_pi_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation applies over Spec Z, since the stages are Noetherian and so qcqs, and S_s is lft over Z, hence lfp. 2) Generators come from the lft definition, and lem-trf-affine-open-limit-descent applies: its hypotheses (cofiltered, affine transitions, qs stages) hold. 3) The helper gives one arrow and lifts of all z_ab, and T'_a is affine by the affine-morphism definition. 4) Open-fibre-product and affine-spectra give e^{-1}(O_a)=V_a, and B (x) A -> C_a is onto from the generators. 5) The affine-cover criterion gives a closed immersion into W. 6) Mc=e, and IsImmersion.of_comp / 07RK(1) needs no hypotheses, so c is an immersion; chart witnesses come from criterion (1). 7) I checked the presentation of the localization B[1/b]. 8) The overlap records are restrictions of one map phi; I accept 'elementary'. This is the 01ZE route. Replacing the directed finite-data lemma is justified because the approximations are indexed by cofiltered categories. NEW NODE: true and statement-only.
